title: Nisaba whole-field compression atlas
thesis: After every source component has a reviewed theorem dependency graph, Phase II may rebuild the mathematics as a smaller graph of reusable ideas while preserving links back to the uncompressed source graphs.
rewritePolicy: We independently rewrite each shared idea in one canonical language. A source-specific presentation survives whenever it carries different mathematics, a useful route, an application, history, or an unresolved editorial choice.
coverageNote: The atlas describes a future compression design; it does not claim the books are already processed. Phase I is complete only when every one of the 717 component files pins an exact edition, inventories every source unit, captures every theorem and supporting result, and has an independently reviewed direct dependency graph. Phase-II Knowledge mappings are not part of that gate.

clusters.title: Objects, statements, functions, and proofs
clusters.canonicalIdea: Mathematics talks about typed objects. Predicates make statements, functions transform objects, and proof rules establish quantified claims under explicit assumptions.
clusters.rewriteDecision: Teach this language once. Later branches add structure, but they do not get private definitions of variable, equality, set, function, implication, or proof.

notationResolutions.resolution: A new name uses :=. Equality compares already meaningful expressions.

routes.label: Minimized canonical route
routes.summary: Use the smallest currently known dependency set for objects, statements, functions, and proofs.

routes.label: Candidate source-route pattern
routes.summary: Set-theoretic and type-theoretic introductions remain source-faithful routes until their foundational equivalence is specified.

residuals.title: Set-theoretic and type-theoretic foundations
residuals.reason: They support much of the same ordinary mathematics but are not literally the same foundational theory.

residuals.title: Author-specific proof templates
residuals.reason: Routine presentational variants become examples of the same small library of proof moves.

clusters.title: Numbers, operations, and algebraic laws
clusters.canonicalIdea: Expressions are built from typed operations governed by laws. Number systems are connected structures, and equation solving uses transformations that preserve solutions.
clusters.rewriteDecision: Unify arithmetic and elementary algebra around lawful rewriting, then reveal groups, rings, fields, and algorithms as added structure rather than a restart.

notationResolutions.resolution: The canonical domain includes 0; positive naturals are stated explicitly.

residuals.title: Finite fields and noncommutative rings

clusters.title: Induction, recursion, and decomposition
clusters.canonicalIdea: Build an object from base cases and constructors, define procedures along that construction, and prove properties by reducing to smaller pieces.
clusters.rewriteDecision: Present induction, recursion, loop invariants, recurrences, and well-founded descent as related schemas with explicit differences.

notationResolutions.resolution: Every indexed family states its domain; implementation indexing is translated.

residuals.title: Bijective, recursive, and generating-function counting

clusters.title: Symmetry, actions, invariants, and quotients
clusters.canonicalIdea: A symmetry acts on objects. Orbits collect equivalent descriptions, invariants survive the action, quotients remove redundancy, and representations linearize actions.
clusters.rewriteDecision: Teach action, orbit, stabilizer, invariant, and quotient as the core; connect geometry, algebra, Fourier analysis, and physics through explicit bridges.

notationResolutions.resolution: Use g·x abstractly and reserve ρ(g)x for a linear representation.

residuals.title: Geometric, algebraic, and probabilistic symmetry

clusters.title: Linearity as a common computational engine
clusters.canonicalIdea: A linear map preserves linear combinations. Coordinates make matrices; duality makes measurements; decompositions reveal independent modes.
clusters.rewriteDecision: Introduce preservation before matrix mechanics and reuse it for derivatives, integrals, expectations, Fourier expansions, least squares, and Markov modes.

clusters.title: Approximation, error, conditioning, and stability
clusters.canonicalIdea: An approximation needs a target, error notion, and convergence claim. Conditioning belongs to the problem; stability measures error added by the method.
clusters.rewriteDecision: Use one error vocabulary across analysis, computation, estimation, and perturbation, but never merge convergence modes without a theorem.

clusters.rewriteDecision: Share state, trajectory, composition, invariance, and stability, then preserve distinct existence theories for recurrences, ODE, PDE, and Markov processes.
